examples.name: Default
examples.summary: A function's arguments from a JSON schema: a text field with a default, an `enum` as a `Select`, an integer with `minimum` and `maximum`, a boolean as a `Switch` and a list of paths, one per line. Defaults seed the value, required fields carry the marker, and each field checks itself when the user leaves it.

examples.name: WithValidation
examples.summary: `validate-on="submit"`: nothing turns red until Save calls `validate()`, which shows every message and focuses the first invalid field. A nested object renders as a fieldset with its own legend, and a server message passed in `errors` by path (`origin.host`) stays on its field until the field is edited.

examples.name: CustomField
examples.summary: A `field:<path>` slot replaces one control and keeps the label, description and messages; `ui` orders the keys and sets a placeholder. `x-multiline` turns a string into a `Textarea`.

examples.name: DynamicFields
examples.summary: `ui[path].when` shows the TTL only while caching is on and a rule's Redirect to only for the redirect behavior; a hidden field is not validated and leaves the value. `ui[path].options` loads the origins from the app as the user types, and `widget: 'repeat'` edits the array of rule objects as fieldsets with Add and Remove.

examples.name: RequestSchema
examples.summary: An OpenAPI request body: `oneOf` with a `discriminator` becomes a choice and the chosen variant's fields, `writeOnly` strings become password fields that keep the stored secret when left empty, `format` checks the email, URL and date, a string map (`additionalProperties`) is edited as key/value rows, and `ui[''].sections` folds the rest under Advanced settings.
